title: The Relationship Between Deliberate Practice and Performance in Sports
method_studied: Accumulated deliberate practice as a predictor of sports performance
finding: Deliberate practice accounted for 18% of variance in sports performance overall and 1% among elite performers. Higher-skill athletes did not start earlier.
effect: 18% of variance overall; 1% among elite-level performers (k and CI absent from abstract)
contested: Ericsson and Harwell 2019 (10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02396) argue the Macnamara meta-analyses used a definition of practice broader than the original.
implication_for_bucket: Treat hours of practice as one input among several and measure skill itself.
notes: Companion to Macnamara 2014, which is already held in career-work.jsonl as deliberate-practice-variance-explained.

title: The role of deliberate practice in expert performance: revisiting Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Römer (1993)
population: Student violinists at three skill levels
method_studied: Double-blind replication of the Ericsson, Krampe and Tesch-Romer 1993 violinist study
finding: The core finding that accumulated deliberate practice matched each skill level did not replicate. The effect was substantial and smaller than in the original, and teacher-designed practice explained no more variance than practice alone.
contested: This paper is the replication failure for Ericsson et al. 1993.
implication_for_bucket: Cite the 1993 violinist result with its failed replication beside it.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: The influence of deliberate practice on musical achievement: a meta-analysis
method_studied: Task-relevant accumulated practice against objectively assessed musical achievement
finding: Accumulated task-relevant practice correlated with musical achievement.
contested: Mosing et al. 2014 (10.1177/0956797614541990) find the practice and ability association in twins to be mostly genetic.
implication_for_bucket: Log structured solo practice time because it predicts achievement in domains with stable tasks.

title: Deliberate Practice and Proposed Limits on the Effects of Practice on the Acquisition of Expert Performance: Why the Original Definition Matters and Recommendations for Future Research
population: Studies from the Macnamara 2014 corpus that meet the original definition of deliberate or purposeful practice
method_studied: Reanalysis restricted to teacher-designed or purposeful practice
finding: Under the original definition, practice explained 29% of variance in performance, or 61% after correction for attenuation, against the 14% reported by Macnamara et al.
effect: 29% of variance (61% after attenuation correction) versus 14% in Macnamara, Hambrick and Oswald
contested: The estimate depends on which studies count as deliberate practice; Macnamara and Maitra 2019 (10.1098/rsos.190327) found teacher-designed practice added nothing over practice alone.
implication_for_bucket: Define a practice activity by its design features and record which definition each metric uses.
notes: The size of the deliberate practice effect is contested in both directions.

title: Does Simulation-Based Medical Education With Deliberate Practice Yield Better Results Than Traditional Clinical Education? A Meta-Analytic Comparative Review of the Evidence
method_studied: Simulation-based medical education with deliberate practice against traditional clinical education
finding: Simulation with deliberate practice beat traditional clinical education on clinical skill acquisition.
effect: Overall effect size 0.71, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.76, P < .001, k = 14
contested: The authors call the number of studies small.
implication_for_bucket: Give working researchers rehearsal of specific skills with feedback before they use them on live work.
notes: The abstract does not name the effect size metric.

title: Systematic Review: The Relationship between Clinical Experience and Quality of Health Care
method_studied: Years in practice against knowledge and quality of care
finding: 32 of 62 evaluations (52%) found performance fell with years in practice on all outcomes; one found it rose on all outcomes.
effect: 52% of 62 evaluations show decreasing performance with experience on all outcomes; 21% no association; 2% increasing on all outcomes
implication_for_bucket: Schedule refreshers and reassessment for experienced users, since years of experience alone do not maintain skill.

title: Practice Does Not Make Perfect
method_studied: Music practice against music ability, with a monozygotic co-twin control
finding: Practice was 40% to 70% heritable. Within identical twin pairs, the twin who practised more showed no better ability.
effect: rs = .18 to .36 between practice and ability; practice heritability 40% to 70%; no within-pair difference for monozygotic twins
implication_for_bucket: Avoid promising that practice volume alone will close ability gaps.
notes: Ability was measured as rhythm, melody and pitch discrimination.

title: The relationship between work experience and job performance: a conceptual and meta‐analytic review
method_studied: Work experience measures against job performance
finding: Experience correlated .27 with job performance. Amount and task-level measures of experience correlated highest.
effect: Estimated population correlation .27; amount measures .43; task-level measures .41; hard criteria .39 versus soft .24
implication_for_bucket: Count task-level repetitions of a skill in preference to years in role.
notes: The abstract prints the main value as 27 with the decimal point dropped.

title: Situated Learning
population: Midwives, tailors, quartermasters, butchers and recovering alcoholics, from ethnographies
method_studied: Legitimate peripheral participation in a community of practitioners
finding: Learning is described as movement from peripheral to full participation in the practices of a community.
contested: Anderson, Reder and Simon 1996 (10.3102/0013189X025004005) argue the central claims of situated learning are overstated.
implication_for_bucket: Give newcomers real low-risk tasks inside a working research group and widen their scope over time.

title: Situated Cognition and the Culture of Learning
population: School learners; two mathematics teaching cases
method_studied: Cognitive apprenticeship as an alternative to abstracted instruction
finding: Knowledge is argued to be partly a product of the activity, context and culture in which it is developed and used.
contested: Anderson, Reder and Simon 1996 (10.3102/0013189X025004005) cite experiments showing transfer across contexts and gains from abstract instruction.
implication_for_bucket: Teach methods inside real research problems and add abstraction, since both have support.

title: Cognitive Apprenticeship: Teaching the Crafts of Reading, Writing, and Mathematics
population: School learners in reading, writing and mathematics
method_studied: Modelling, coaching, scaffolding, articulation, reflection and exploration
finding: The chapter adapts craft apprenticeship to cognitive skills by bringing tacit expert processes into the open where learners can observe and practise them.
implication_for_bucket: Show expert reasoning step by step, coach the learner through the same steps, then withdraw support.
notes: Chapter by Collins, Brown and Newman, first published 1989 in Knowing, Learning, and Instruction (Erlbaum). Crossref holds the 2018 Routledge reissue.

title: Situated Learning and Education
method_studied: Test of four claims of situated learning
finding: The authors cite empirical work to show that the claims that knowledge does not transfer, that abstract training is of little use and that instruction must be social and complex are overstated.
implication_for_bucket: Combine situated practice with explicit abstract instruction and part-task drills.

title: Cognitive apprenticeship in health sciences education: a qualitative review
population: Health sciences education, 104 articles categorised, 26 synthesised
method_studied: Use of cognitive apprenticeship theory in design and analysis
finding: Applications concentrated on the methods dimension such as coaching and scaffolding; the review is qualitative and reports no outcome effect.
contested: The review found 45 of 149 articles cited the theory only in the reference list.
implication_for_bucket: Label cognitive apprenticeship as a design frame whose outcome evidence is thin.
notes: Abstract from Europe PMC.

title: Cognitive Apprenticeship in STEM Graduate Education: A Qualitative Review of the Literature
method_studied: Cognitive apprenticeship framework used by faculty
finding: The review judges the framework useful for helping faculty build learning opportunities for graduate students; evidence is qualitative.
implication_for_bucket: Offer advisors a checklist of modelling, coaching and fading moves and test whether it changes student skill.

title: The Tacit Dimension
venue: Doubleday; University of Chicago Press reissue
method_studied: Tacit knowing
finding: The book that introduced the tacit dimension of knowledge to the later literature.
contested: Eraut 2000 (10.1348/000709900158001) sets out the multiple meanings later given to tacit knowledge and the difficulty of detecting and representing it.
implication_for_bucket: State which kind of unarticulated knowledge a feature targets before claiming to transfer it.
notes: No DOI found. Confirmed as Michael Polanyi, The Tacit Dimension, first published 1966, through Open Library. Content summary is limited to what the catalogue record supports.

title: A Dynamic Theory of Organizational Knowledge Creation
method_studied: Four patterns of interaction between tacit and explicit knowledge
finding: Organizational knowledge is proposed to arise from continuous dialogue between tacit and explicit knowledge.
contested: Gourlay 2006 (10.1111/j.1467-6486.2006.00637.x) argues the conversion modes lack evidence that a plainer account cannot explain.
implication_for_bucket: Treat tacit to explicit conversion as a hypothesis and test whether written protocols reproduce a skill.

title: Conceptualizing Knowledge Creation: A Critique of Nonaka's Theory
method_studied: Evidence behind the four modes of knowledge conversion
finding: Three of the modes appear plausible and none is supported by evidence that cannot be explained by a simpler account.
implication_for_bucket: Avoid building product claims on the SECI model.

title: Tacit Knowledge, Trust and the Q of Sapphire
population: Physicists measuring the quality factor of sapphire in Russia, the USA and Glasgow
method_studied: Fieldwork on reproducing a measurement across labs
finding: Western labs took about 20 years to repeat the Russian measurement, and shortfalls in tacit knowledge were partly responsible. Personal contact between scientists carried the missing knowledge.
implication_for_bucket: Add fields to methods records for details that experimenters learn only by contact, such as how long a step took.
notes: Case study; one measurement.

title: Tacit and Explicit Knowledge
method_studied: Classification of tacit knowledge
finding: Book on tacit and explicit knowledge. No abstract could be fetched, so the content is not summarised here.
implication_for_bucket: Read the book before using its categories in product design.
notes: No abstract in Crossref or OpenAlex, so the finding is limited to the title-level description.

title: Exploring internal stickiness: Impediments to the transfer of best practice within the firm
population: 122 best-practice transfers in eight companies, 271 observations
method_studied: Barriers to internal transfer of practices
finding: The main barriers were knowledge-related: low absorptive capacity of the recipient, causal ambiguity and an arduous relationship between source and recipient. Motivation mattered less.
implication_for_bucket: Check prerequisite knowledge of the recipient before a method handover and keep source and recipient in contact.
notes: Canonical correlation analysis; coefficients are absent from the abstract.

title: Inter‐ and Intra‐Organizational Knowledge Transfer: A Meta‐Analytic Review and Assessment of its Antecedents and Consequences
method_studied: Antecedents and consequences of organizational knowledge transfer
finding: Knowledge, organization and network characteristics each relate to transfer, and context and direction moderate the relationships.
implication_for_bucket: Record tie strength and context when studying whether a method spreads between labs.
notes: Effect null: The fetched abstract states no pooled number.

title: Non‐formal learning and tacit knowledge in professional work
population: Professionals studied in several empirical projects
method_studied: Typology of non-formal learning: implicit, reactive and deliberative
finding: Tacit knowledge is hard both to detect and to represent. Professional performance combines routinised action with rapid intuitive decisions, and periods of deliberation keep critical control.
implication_for_bucket: Build short deliberate review points into fast routine work.

title: Informal learning in the workplace
population: Early and mid-career professionals in a series of projects
method_studied: Frameworks for what is learned at work, how, and what shapes the effort
finding: The paper deconstructs informal learning, learning from experience, tacit knowledge and transfer into the distinct phenomena each term covers.
implication_for_bucket: Design for learning that happens as a by-product of work: allocation of tasks, challenge and access to colleagues.

title: Informal and Incidental Learning
venue: New Directions for Adult and Continuing Education
method_studied: Theory of informal and incidental learning
finding: Updates the Marsick and Watkins theory of informal and incidental learning.
implication_for_bucket: Prompt reflection after routine events, since incidental learning can go unexamined.
notes: The abstract is one sentence.

title: Antecedents and Outcomes of Informal Learning Behaviors: a Meta-Analysis
method_studied: Informal learning behaviours and their correlates
finding: Engagement in informal learning behaviours correlated with attitudes, knowledge and skill acquisition, and performance.
effect: rho = .29 attitudes; rho = .41 knowledge/skill acquisition; rho = .42 performance; k = 49, N = 55,514
contested: Correlational; the abstract repeats the 70% to 90% informal learning figure that Clardy 2018 (10.1177/1534484318759399) finds unsupported.
implication_for_bucket: Support self-directed learning on the job and state that the link to performance is correlational.
notes: Abstract fetched from the Springer article page.

title: 70-20-10 and the Dominance of Informal Learning: A Fact in Search of Evidence
population: Five literature traditions behind the 70% informal learning claim
method_studied: Critical review of the evidential basis
finding: The evidence for the claim that 70% or more of work learning is informal is weak, with sloppy scholarship, inconsistent concepts and protocol problems. The author recommends setting the rule aside.
implication_for_bucket: Drop the 70-20-10 ratio from product copy and design.

title: The 70:20:10 framework and the transfer of learning
population: Middle managers in the Australian public sector
method_studied: Implementation of the 70:20:10 framework
finding: Programmes built on 70:20:10 did not achieve the intended transfer. One cause was the assumption that unstructured experience develops capability by itself.
implication_for_bucket: Structure on-the-job learning with goals, support and review.

title: The Lessons of Experience: How Successful Executives Develop on the Job
method_studied: Retrospective accounts of developmental job experiences
finding: The Center for Creative Leadership study from which the 70-20-10 ratio is often derived.
contested: Clardy 2018 (10.1177/1534484318759399) finds the evidential basis of the 70% rule weak.
implication_for_bucket: Cite this book as the origin of an unverified ratio.
notes: No DOI. Confirmed as McCall, Lombardo and Morrison, The Lessons of Experience, Lexington Books 1988, through OpenAlex W613326940 and Open Library. The link between this book and the ratio is the usual attribution; the text was not fetched.

title: Effectiveness of training in organizations: A meta-analysis of design and evaluation features.
method_studied: Training design and evaluation features
finding: Organizational training showed medium to large effects on all four Kirkpatrick criteria.
implication_for_bucket: Measure behaviour and results as well as learning; formal training has measurable effects on each.

title: Leadership training design, delivery, and implementation: A meta-analysis.
method_studied: Leadership training design, delivery and implementation
finding: Leadership training improved reactions, learning, transfer and results, with size depending on design and delivery.
effect: delta = .63 reactions; .73 learning; .82 transfer; .72 results; 335 samples
implication_for_bucket: Include practice and feedback in soft-skill modules and track transfer.

title: The effects of feedback interventions on performance: A historical review, a meta-analysis, and a preliminary feedback intervention theory.
method_studied: Feedback interventions
finding: Feedback improved performance on average and over one third of interventions lowered it. Effectiveness fell as feedback drew attention toward the self and away from the task.
effect: d = .41; 607 effect sizes; 23,663 observations; over 1/3 of interventions decreased performance
contested: The authors state the moderating task characteristics are poorly understood.
implication_for_bucket: Keep feedback on the task and the next step; avoid comments about the person.

title: Does performance improve following multisource feedback? a theoretical model, meta‐analysis, and review of empirical findings
method_studied: Multisource (360-degree) feedback
finding: Improvement in direct report, peer and supervisor ratings after multisource feedback was small.
implication_for_bucket: Pair any peer feedback feature with goal setting and a follow-up action.
notes: Effect null: the abstract says improvement is small and gives no number.

title: How Are We Doing After 30 Years? A Meta-Analytic Review of the Antecedents and Outcomes of Feedback-Seeking Behavior
method_studied: Antecedents and outcomes of feedback-seeking behaviour
finding: Tenure and age related negatively to feedback seeking, and the relationship between feedback seeking and performance was small.
implication_for_bucket: Deliver feedback by default for senior users, who seek it less.
notes: Effect null: The fetched abstract states no pooled number.

title: Audit and feedback: effects on professional practice and healthcare outcomes
method_studied: Audit and feedback against usual care
finding: Audit and feedback produced a small median improvement in compliance with desired practice, with wide variation.
effect: Weighted median adjusted risk difference 4.3% absolute increase in compliance (IQR 0.5% to 16%), 82 comparisons from 49 studies; continuous outcomes 1.3% (IQR 1.3% to 28.9%)
contested: Crossref marks a newer version of this Cochrane review.
implication_for_bucket: Expect small average gains from performance dashboards and test formats that raise them.

title: A Quantitative Review of Performance Feedback in Organizational Settings (1998-2018)
method_studied: Performance feedback in organizational behaviour management
finding: Feedback produced large effects across applications, including those meeting What Works Clearinghouse standards.
contested: Drawn from four journals; Kluger and DeNisi 1996 (10.1037/0033-2909.119.2.254) report a smaller average, with over one third of interventions lowering performance.
implication_for_bucket: Use frequent, specific, behaviour-level feedback and verify with controlled tests.
notes: Effect null: the abstract says large and gives no number.

title: Do Team and Individual Debriefs Enhance Performance? A Meta-Analysis
venue: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
method_studied: Debriefs or after-action reviews against control
finding: Debriefs improved effectiveness by about 25%, with similar effects for teams and individuals and for simulated and real settings.
effect: d = .67; 46 samples; N = 2,136; about 25% improvement over control
implication_for_bucket: Build a short structured debrief into the end of each experiment or project.

title: A meta-analysis of the effectiveness of the after-action review (or debrief) and factors that influence its effectiveness.
population: Trainees in 61 studies, 915 teams and 3,499 individuals, in military, healthcare and other settings
method_studied: After-action review characteristics
finding: The after-action review was effective overall. Alignment to the individual or team and objective review media contributed most.
effect: d = 0.79 overall (61 studies, 107 effect sizes, 915 teams and 3,499 individuals)
implication_for_bucket: Base debriefs on objective records of what happened, such as logs or recordings.
notes: Effect read from the full abstract at Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar on 2026-10-11. The OpenAlex abstract begins mid-sentence at a figure that belongs to Tannenbaum and Cerasoli, which an earlier pass misread as the overall effect of this paper.

title: Effectiveness of error management training: A meta-analysis.
method_studied: Error management training against error-avoidant training
finding: Encouraging errors during training improved performance, most for transfer to structurally new tasks.
effect: d = 0.44 overall (k = 24, N = 2,183); 0.56 post-training transfer; 0.80 adaptive transfer
implication_for_bucket: Let learners explore and make errors in practice when the goal is adaptation to new problems.

title: Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams
population: 51 work teams in a manufacturing company
method_studied: Team psychological safety and learning behaviour
finding: Team psychological safety was associated with learning behaviour, which mediated its link to team performance.
implication_for_bucket: Make it safe to report failed experiments inside a group.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no coefficient.

title: Psychological Safety: A Meta‐Analytic Review and Extension
population: 136 independent samples, over 22,000 individuals and nearly 5,000 groups
method_studied: Antecedents and outcomes of psychological safety
finding: Psychological safety relates to task performance and citizenship beyond related constructs.
implication_for_bucket: Track psychological safety as a condition for error reporting.
notes: Effect null: The fetched abstract states no pooled number.

title: After-Event Reviews: Drawing Lessons From Successful and Failed Experience.
method_studied: Reviews of both successes and failures against reviews of failures only
finding: Soldiers debriefed on successes and failures improved more than those who reviewed failures only.
implication_for_bucket: Review what worked as well as what failed.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: A quasi-experimental study of after-event reviews and leadership development.
population: 173 participants followed for 9 months across 4 developmental experiences
method_studied: Structured after-event reviews
finding: After-event reviews improved leadership development, more for conscientious, open and emotionally stable people with rich prior experience.
implication_for_bucket: Add structured reflection prompts after each major project.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Not Learning From Failure—the Greatest Failure of All
method_studied: Failure feedback against success feedback on binary-choice questions
finding: People learned less from failure feedback than from success feedback, and learned equally from the failures and successes of others.
implication_for_bucket: Present errors in a low-ego frame, for example through the errors of other people.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no effect size. The tasks were binary-choice questions.

title: Transfer of training: a review and directions for future research
method_studied: Training design, trainee and work-environment factors
finding: The review defines transfer as generalization to the job plus maintenance over time and sets out the three-input model.
implication_for_bucket: Measure both generalization and maintenance of a trained skill.

title: Transfer of Training: A Meta-Analytic Review
method_studied: Predictors of transfer
finding: Cognitive ability, conscientiousness, motivation and a supportive work environment predicted transfer, more for open skills. Same-source, same-context measurement inflated relationships.
contested: The authors report that same-source measurement inflates transfer estimates.
implication_for_bucket: Measure transfer with a source other than the learner and expect weaker transfer for open skills.
notes: Journal issue dated 2010; Crossref issued date is 2009. Effect null: the abstract gives no coefficient.

title: Does Far Transfer Exist? Negative Evidence From Chess, Music, and Working Memory Training
population: Children in chess, music and working memory training studies
method_studied: Far transfer to cognitive and academic skills
finding: Effects were small to moderate and shrank as design quality rose. The authors conclude far transfer rarely occurs.
implication_for_bucket: Train the target research skills themselves.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: An investigation of training activities and transfer of training in organizations
method_studied: Transfer activities before, during and after training
finding: Reported application of training fell over time. Activities in the work environment before and after training related more to transfer than activities during it.
effect: 62%, 44% and 34% of employees apply training immediately, six months and one year after
contested: Figures are estimates by training professionals.
implication_for_bucket: Schedule follow-up in the workplace after any course.

title: A Meta-Analytic Review of Behavior Modeling Training.
method_studied: Behaviour modelling training
finding: Effects were largest for learning, smaller for job behaviour and smaller again for results. Transfer was greatest with mixed models, trainee-generated scenarios, goal setting and trained supervisors.
implication_for_bucket: Show both good and bad worked examples and have learners practise on their own scenarios.
notes: Effect null: The fetched abstract states no pooled number.

title: Career Benefits Associated With Mentoring for Proteges: A Meta-Analysis.
method_studied: Mentored against non-mentored; mentoring received
finding: Mentoring was associated with career benefits, and effect sizes for objective outcomes such as compensation were small.
contested: Kammeyer-Mueller and Judge 2008 (10.1016/j.jvb.2007.09.006) note many mentoring and outcome relationships may be spurious.
implication_for_bucket: Present mentoring as a modest contributor to objective career outcomes.
notes: Effect null: The fetched abstract states no pooled number.

title: Does mentoring matter? A multidisciplinary meta-analysis comparing mentored and non-mentored individuals
method_studied: Mentored against non-mentored individuals
finding: Mentoring was associated with favourable outcomes of many kinds, and the effect size was generally small. Academic and workplace mentoring showed larger effects than youth mentoring.
implication_for_bucket: Set expectations for mentor matching at small average effects.
notes: Abstract from Europe PMC. Effect null: The fetched abstract states no pooled number.

title: An interdisciplinary meta-analysis of the potential antecedents, correlates, and consequences of protégé perceptions of mentoring.
method_studied: Protege perceptions of instrumental support, psychosocial support and relationship quality
finding: Similarity in attitudes, values, beliefs and personality was the strongest correlate of positive protege perceptions.
effect: rho = .38 to .59 for deep-level similarity; instrumental support with situational satisfaction rho = .36; relationship quality rho = .38
contested: Perceptions are self-reported.
implication_for_bucket: Match mentors on values and working style as well as on topic.

title: Mentorship and protégé success in STEM fields
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
method_studied: Mentor characteristics from genealogy data
finding: Mentorship was associated with a rise in the likelihood of prizewinning, NAS induction or superstardom relative to matched proteges.
effect: 2x to 4x rise in likelihood; models explain 34% to 44% of variance in protege success
contested: Observational with matching; selection of proteges by mentors remains possible.
implication_for_bucket: Help early-career researchers reach mentors and state that the size of the causal part is unknown.

title: Intellectual synthesis in mentorship determines success in academic careers
population: 18,856 researchers with graduate and postdoctoral training, mostly neuroscience
method_studied: Mentor expertise and trainee synthesis of it
finding: Postdoctoral mentors predicted trainee success more than graduate mentors. Trainees who combined the differing expertise of their mentors were more likely to continue in academia.
implication_for_bucket: Encourage researchers to train under mentors with different expertise and to combine the two.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Superstar Extinction
population: Coauthors of 112 academic superstars who died unexpectedly
method_studied: Loss of a star collaborator
finding: Collaborators suffered a lasting decline in quality-adjusted publication rates after the death of the star.
effect: 5% to 8% lasting decline in quality-adjusted publication rate
implication_for_bucket: Treat access to leading people in a field as a source of ideas that a product can widen.

title: Quality Matters: The Expulsion of Professors and the Consequences for PhD Student Outcomes in Nazi Germany
population: Mathematics PhD students in Germany before and after the dismissals of 1933
method_studied: Faculty quality, instrumented by the expulsion of professors
finding: Faculty quality determined short-run and long-run PhD student outcomes.
effect: One SD rise in faculty quality: +13 percentage points probability of publishing the dissertation in a top journal; +10 points becoming full professor; +16 points positive lifetime citations; +6.3 lifetime citations
contested: One field and one historical setting.
implication_for_bucket: Help applicants weigh advisor and department quality when choosing a PhD.

title: Can Mentoring Help Female Assistant Professors in Economics? An Evaluation by Randomized Trial
method_studied: CeMENT mentoring workshop
finding: Treated women were more likely to stay in academia and to hold tenure at an institution ranked in the top 30 or 50 in economics.
implication_for_bucket: Run group mentoring workshops for early-career researchers; this design has trial evidence.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Early-career setback and future career impact
population: Junior scientists near the NIH R01 funding threshold
method_studied: Near miss against narrow win
finding: A near miss predicted more than a 10% chance of leaving the NIH system for good, and those who stayed outperformed narrow winners in the longer run.
effect: More than a 10% chance of disappearing permanently from the NIH system after a near miss
implication_for_bucket: Support researchers through early rejection, when dropout risk is highest.

title: A theory of vocational choice.
method_studied: Person and environment types
finding: The founding statement of the Holland theory of vocational choice.
contested: Hoff et al. 2020 (10.1016/j.jvb.2020.103503) report that earlier meta-analyses found non-significant relations between interest fit and job satisfaction.
implication_for_bucket: Use interest fit as one weak signal in career guidance.

title: Are you interested? A meta-analysis of relations between vocational interests and employee performance and turnover.
method_studied: Vocational interests against performance and turnover
finding: Single interest scales had small validities, larger when the scale matched the specific job.
effect: .14 job performance; .26 training performance; -.19 turnover intentions; -.15 actual turnover; job-specific scales .23 for job performance versus .10 for single RIASEC interests
implication_for_bucket: Match interests to the specific role when predicting fit.
notes: Validities corrected for criterion unreliability only.

title: Vocational Interests and Performance
method_studied: Interests and congruence indices against performance and persistence
finding: Interests related to performance and persistence, and congruence indices correlated more strongly than interest scores alone.
implication_for_bucket: Score fit between a person and an environment as well as raw interest.
notes: Effect null: The fetched abstract states no pooled number.

title: Interest fit and job satisfaction: A systematic review and meta-analysis
method_studied: Interest fit against job satisfaction
finding: Interest fit related positively and weakly to job satisfaction, and more strongly to satisfaction with career choice.
implication_for_bucket: Tell users that interest fit explains a small share of job satisfaction.
notes: Abstract from Semantic Scholar.

title: Toward a Unifying Social Cognitive Theory of Career and Academic Interest, Choice, and Performance
method_studied: Self-efficacy, outcome expectations and goals
finding: The founding statement of social cognitive career theory.
implication_for_bucket: Build self-efficacy through mastery experiences in the target field.
notes: Abstract from ERIC.

title: Predictors of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics choice options: A meta-analytic path analysis of the social–cognitive choice model by gender and race/ethnicity.
method_studied: SCCT interest and choice model in STEM
finding: The model fit across gender and racial and ethnic groups and explained large portions of variance in interests and choice goals.
implication_for_bucket: Track self-efficacy and outcome expectations as leading indicators of persistence in research.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no coefficient.

title: Planned Happenstance: Constructing Unexpected Career Opportunities
method_studied: Exploratory action to create and use unplanned events
finding: Unplanned events are treated as inevitable and desirable, and counsellors should teach clients to generate and use them.
contested: The paper is a counselling proposal and its abstract reports no outcome data.
implication_for_bucket: Encourage exploration and exposure to new groups, and label the idea as theory.

title: Career Adapt-Abilities Scale: Construction, reliability, and measurement equivalence across 13 countries
method_studied: Career Adapt-Abilities Scale: concern, control, curiosity, confidence
finding: The paper that constructed the scale and tested measurement equivalence across 13 countries.
implication_for_bucket: Use the scale if career adaptability is measured.
notes: Effect null: Abstract text was unavailable from Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC and ERIC, so no number is recorded.

title: Career adaptability: A meta-analysis of relationships with measures of adaptivity, adapting responses, and adaptation results
method_studied: Career adaptability against adaptivity, adapting responses and adaptation results
finding: Meta-analysis of career adaptability correlates.
implication_for_bucket: Hold claims about career adaptability until the numbers are read from the paper.
notes: Effect null: Abstract text was unavailable from Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC and ERIC, so no number is recorded.

title: Effectiveness of career choice interventions: A meta-analytic replication and extension
method_studied: Career choice interventions
finding: Meta-analytic replication and extension of earlier findings on career choice interventions.
implication_for_bucket: Read the full text before citing an effect for career interventions.
notes: Effect null: Abstract text was unavailable from Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC and ERIC, so no number is recorded.

title: Effectiveness of job search interventions: A meta-analytic review.
population: Job seekers in 47 experimental or quasi-experimental evaluations
method_studied: Job search interventions
finding: Participants in job search interventions had higher odds of obtaining employment than controls.
effect: Odds of obtaining employment 2.67 times higher; 47 interventions
implication_for_bucket: Teach job search skills and goal setting; this intervention class has the strongest career evidence found here.

title: Skill Formation and the Economics of Investing in Disadvantaged Children
population: Review of child and adult intervention evidence
method_studied: Life cycle skill formation
finding: Skill formation is a dynamic process in which early inputs raise the productivity of later inputs.
implication_for_bucket: Sequence learning so that foundations come first, since earlier skills raise the return on later ones.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: The Technology of Skill Formation
method_studied: Stage-specific technology with self-productivity and dynamic complementarity
finding: A model of skill formation with self-productivity, dynamic complementarity and skill multipliers.
implication_for_bucket: Model prerequisites as a graph, since skills build on skills.

title: Why Do Firms Train? Theory and Evidence
method_studied: Employer information advantage and general training
finding: Employers pay for general training when they know more about worker ability than outside firms do. German apprentice microdata give the model some support.
implication_for_bucket: Expect employers to fund general skills only where they can retain the trained worker.

title: What Works? A Meta Analysis of Recent Active Labor Market Program Evaluations
venue: Journal of the European Economic Association
population: Over 200 evaluations of active labour market programmes
method_studied: Training, job search assistance and subsidies
finding: Average impacts were near zero in the short run and more positive two to three years after completion, with larger gains for human capital programmes.
implication_for_bucket: Evaluate learning outcomes at two to three years as well as at completion.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no pooled number.

title: An alternative approach to estimate the wage returns to private‐sector training
population: Workers who wanted training, some prevented by a random event
method_studied: Private-sector training
finding: As the comparison group narrowed to workers who planned training and missed it for a random reason, the estimated wage return fell from large and significant to near zero.
implication_for_bucket: Discount observational estimates of returns to training for selection.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Why Do Sectoral Employment Programs Work? Lessons from WorkAdvance
population: Low-wage workers in randomised evaluations of sector-focused training
method_studied: Screening, occupational and soft-skills training and wraparound services
finding: Sectoral programmes generated persistent earnings gains by moving participants into higher-wage jobs.
effect: Earnings gains of 12% to 34% following training
implication_for_bucket: Tie training to certifiable skills that a specific sector hires for.
notes: Review of randomised evaluations plus analysis of WorkAdvance.

title: Wage Effects of On‐the‐Job Training: A Meta‐Analysis
method_studied: On-the-job training courses
finding: The average wage effect of on-the-job training was small after correction for publication bias, and lower in studies that corrected for selection.
effect: 2.6% wage effect per course, corrected for publication bias
implication_for_bucket: Quote a modest wage return for a single course.

title: Returns to Apprenticeship Training in Austria: Evidence from Failed Firms
population: Apprentices in small Austrian firms that failed
method_studied: Length of apprenticeship, instrumented by time to firm failure
finding: Instrumental variable returns to apprenticeship were similar to or larger than OLS returns, which indicates little selection.
implication_for_bucket: Treat time spent in apprenticeship as having a causal return on earnings.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Toward an Understanding of Learning by Doing: Evidence from an Automobile Assembly Plant
method_studied: Learning by doing on a production line
finding: Most knowledge gained through production was not retained by the plant workers, which the authors find consistent with the plant systems for productivity measurement and improvement.
implication_for_bucket: Capture what a team learns in shared records, since much of it sits in systems.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Undergraduate research experiences: Impacts and opportunities
method_studied: Research experiences
finding: Evidence that research experiences improve participation and persistence is weak; more than half the studies rely on self-report surveys or interviews.
implication_for_bucket: Assess research skill with performance measures.

title: Making a Difference in Science Education
method_studied: Undergraduate research programme participation, with propensity score matching
finding: Participation raised the probability of planning to enrol in a STEM graduate programme.
contested: The outcome is stated intention.
implication_for_bucket: Track enrolment and persistence as well as intention.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Postdocs’ lab engagement predicts trajectories of PhD students’ skill development
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
population: 336 PhD students in the United States, longitudinal
method_studied: Lab engagement of PIs, postdocs and senior students
finding: PI lab and mentoring activity did not predict student skill trajectories. Active participation of postdocs and senior students in lab discussion did.
effect: Junior PhD students over 4 times as likely to have positive skill development trajectories
implication_for_bucket: Connect junior researchers with near peers one or two stages ahead.

title: Graduate Students’ Teaching Experiences Improve Their Methodological Research Skills
method_studied: Teaching plus research against research only
finding: Students who both taught and did research improved more in generating testable hypotheses and designing valid experiments.
implication_for_bucket: Have researchers teach or explain methods to others as practice.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Doctoring Uncertainty:
population: Doctoral students in laboratory and field sciences
method_studied: Socialisation into research
finding: Doctoral students learn that research does not produce stable results until they master tacit craft skills, then learn to remove that work from public accounts.
implication_for_bucket: Prepare new researchers for failure of routine experiments and record the craft fixes.

title: Early Engagement in Course-Based Research Increases Graduation Rates and Completion of Science, Engineering, and Mathematics Degrees
population: First-year undergraduates in the Freshman Research Initiative
method_studied: Three-semester course-based research, with propensity score matching
finding: Students who completed all three semesters were more likely to earn a STEM degree and graduate within six years. Grade point average was unaffected.
implication_for_bucket: Offer research experience inside courses to reach more people.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Undergraduate Research Experiences Broaden Diversity in the Scientific Workforce
population: Underrepresented science students followed for 10 years, propensity score matched
method_studied: Duration and intensity of faculty-mentored research
finding: Only students who did 10 or more hours a week for two or more semesters were more likely to graduate in science, enter graduate training and work in science six years later.
effect: Threshold: 10 or more hours per week across two or more semesters or summers
implication_for_bucket: Design research experiences to last at least two terms at ten hours a week.

title: Academic breeding grounds: Home department conditions and early career performance of academic researchers
population: A cohort of Swedish doctoral graduates in science, engineering, mathematics and medicine
method_studied: Research group size and funding conditions
finding: PhD students trained in groups with fewer PhD students were more productive afterwards.
implication_for_bucket: Flag group size and supervision ratio to applicants choosing a lab.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Sustainable development of science and scientists: Academic training in life science labs
population: 162 supervising professors and their 791 PhD students in Japanese life science labs
method_studied: Autonomy and exploration in training
finding: Autonomy granted to PhD students improved their long-term performance and lowered short-term performance, which gives supervisors an incentive against it.
implication_for_bucket: Give trainees autonomy over part of their project and judge the result over years.
notes: Abstract from Semantic Scholar. Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Generative AI at Work
method_studied: Staggered introduction of a generative AI conversational assistant
finding: AI assistance raised issues resolved per hour, most for less experienced and lower-skilled workers. The most skilled saw small speed gains and small quality declines. The paper reports evidence of worker learning.
effect: 15% average increase in issues resolved per hour
contested: One occupation: customer support.
implication_for_bucket: Expect the largest AI gains for novices and check quality for experts.

title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
method_studied: GitHub Copilot on one task: an HTTP server in JavaScript
finding: The treatment group finished the task faster than control.
effect: 55.8% faster task completion
contested: Preprint; one bounded task. Becker et al. 2025 (10.48550/arXiv.2507.09089) find a 19% slowdown for experienced developers in mature projects.
implication_for_bucket: Report AI speed gains with the task type and user experience attached.
notes: Verified through OpenAlex; Crossref does not hold arXiv DOIs.

title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
population: 4,867 developers at Microsoft, Accenture and a Fortune 100 firm
method_studied: Access to an AI coding assistant
finding: Pooled across three noisy experiments, developers with the tool completed more tasks. Less experienced developers adopted more and gained more.
effect: 26.08% increase in completed tasks (SE 10.3%), 4,867 developers
contested: The authors call each experiment noisy with results that vary.
implication_for_bucket: Expect wide uncertainty around AI productivity gains in real teams.

title: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise
method_studied: AI use crossed with individual or team work on product innovation tasks
finding: Individuals with AI matched the performance of teams without AI, and AI users produced solutions balanced across technical and commercial content.
contested: Working paper.
implication_for_bucket: Use AI to widen the range of expertise a single researcher can draw on.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no effect size. The earlier Dell'Acqua 2023 study is already in literature.jsonl.

title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
population: 25,000 workers in 7,000 Danish workplaces across 11 exposed occupations
method_studied: AI chatbot adoption, difference-in-differences
finding: AI chatbots had no significant effect on earnings or recorded hours in any occupation.
effect: Confidence intervals rule out effects larger than 1%; average time savings 3%
contested: Working paper; covers 2023 and 2024.
implication_for_bucket: Separate task-level speed gains from career or earnings outcomes.
notes: Crossref holds this NBER number under the title Still Waters, Rapid Currents; the SSRN version is titled Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
population: 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 tasks in their own mature projects
method_studied: Early-2025 AI tools allowed or disallowed per task
finding: Allowing AI increased completion time, while developers believed it had sped them up.
effect: 19% longer completion time with AI; developers forecast 24% shorter and afterwards estimated 20% shorter
contested: Preprint; 16 developers.
implication_for_bucket: Measure time and quality with logs, since self-reported AI speedup can be wrong in sign.

title: How AI Impacts Skill Formation
population: Developers learning a new asynchronous programming library
method_studied: AI assistance while learning
finding: AI use impaired conceptual understanding, code reading and debugging without significant average efficiency gains. Interaction patterns that kept the learner cognitively engaged preserved learning.
contested: Preprint.
implication_for_bucket: Make the AI ask for the learner's reasoning and explain concepts while a skill is being learned.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Scientific Discovery, and Product Innovation
population: Claimed: 1,018 scientists in a US firm R&D lab
method_studied: AI materials discovery tool
finding: Withdrawn. The paper claimed 44% more materials discovered and 39% more patent filings.
contested: arXiv administrators withdrew the paper over concerns about the validity of the data and incomplete Institutional Review Board requirements (arXiv comment field for 2412.17866).
implication_for_bucket: Exclude this paper from any evidence base and check for withdrawals before citing preprints.
notes: Kept as a warning record. Effect set to null because the data are not trusted.

title: Endoscopist deskilling risk after exposure to artificial intelligence in colonoscopy: a multicentre, observational study
population: 1,443 patients having non-AI colonoscopy before and after AI was introduced
method_studied: Exposure of endoscopists to AI polyp detection
finding: The adenoma detection rate of standard colonoscopy fell after endoscopists had been exposed to AI.
effect: ADR 28.4% (226 of 795) before versus 22.4% (145 of 648) after; absolute difference -6.0% (95% CI -10.5 to -1.6; p = 0.0089); OR 0.69 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.89)
contested: Before and after observational design with three-month windows.
implication_for_bucket: Keep regular unaided practice of any skill the user must retain.
notes: Abstract from Semantic Scholar.

title: Ironies of automation
method_studied: Automation of control tasks
finding: Automation of industrial processes may expand the problems of the human operator instead of removing them.
implication_for_bucket: Plan how users will keep the skills needed to check and override the AI.
notes: Finding taken from the Semantic Scholar summary; no abstract was available.

title: The Retention of Manual Flying Skills in the Automated Cockpit
venue: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
population: 16 airline pilots in a Boeing 747-400 simulator
method_studied: Level of cockpit automation
finding: Instrument scanning and manual control were mostly intact, and the cognitive tasks of manual flight showed more frequent and significant problems.
contested: Sample of 16.
implication_for_bucket: Protect the planning and tracking parts of a task when automating; they decay first.
notes: Effect null: the abstract gives no number.

title: Automation Bias in Mammography: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence                     BI-RADS Suggestions on Reader Performance
method_studied: Correct or incorrect suggestions from a purported AI
finding: Accuracy fell when the AI suggestion was wrong, for every experience level, and inexperienced readers followed wrong suggestions most.
effect: Correct ratings with correct versus incorrect AI suggestion: inexperienced 79.7% versus 19.8%; moderately experienced 81.3% versus 24.8%; very experienced 82.3% versus 45.5%
contested: 27 readers.
implication_for_bucket: Show AI suggestions after the user commits a first judgement on tasks they must be able to check.
notes: Prospective experiment with randomised sets.
